reductionDefinition:
This Sipsers reduction converts the Clique problem into a Vertex Cover problem.
                                            This is done by first taking all possible edges in the original clique graph, and removing
                                            the edges that are actually in the clique graph from that set.
source: Sipser, Michael. Introduction to the Theory of Computation.ACM Sigact News 27.1 (1996): 27-29.

reductionFrom.formalDefinition: Clique = {<G, k> | G is an graph that has a set of k mutually adjacent nodes}
reductionFrom.problemDefinition: A clique is the problem of uncovering a subset of vertices in an undirected graph G = (V, E) such that every two distinct vertices are adjacent
reductionFrom.inputDescription: G, a graph, and k, the size of clique to find
reductionFrom.outputDescription: True or False, whether G contains a clique of size k
reductionFrom.source: Karp, Richard M. Reducibility among combinatorial problems. Complexity of computer computations. Springer, Boston, MA, 1972. 85-103.

defaultSolver.solverDefinition: This is a brute force solver for the NP-Complete Clique problem

defaultVerifier.verifierDefinition: This is a verifier for Clique

defaultVisualization.visualizationDefinition: This is a default visualization for Clique

solver.solverDefinition: This is a brute force solver for the NP-Complete Clique problem

reductionTo.formalDefinition: VERTEXCOVER = {<G, k> | G in an undirected graph that has a k-node vertex cover}
reductionTo.problemDefinition: A vertex cover is a subset of nodes S, such that every edge in the graph, G, touches a node in S.
reductionTo.inputDescription: G, a graph, and k, the target vertex cover size
reductionTo.outputDescription: True or False, whether the given set of nodes is a vertex cover of G
reductionTo.source: Karp, Richard M. Reducibility among combinatorial problems. Complexity of computer computations. Springer, Boston, MA, 1972. 85-103.
reductionTo.instanceFormat: Graph and target cover size, shaped as ((nodes, edges), k). Nodes are a brace-delimited comma-separated list {n1,n2,...}; edges are a brace-delimited list of undirected pairs {{n1,n2},{n2,n3},...} drawn from the node set; k is the required vertex-cover size. Example: (({a,b,c,d},{{a,b},{a,c},{a,d}}),1)
reductionTo.certificateFormat: Comma-separated node names, optionally wrapped in braces. Must name nodes from the instance's node set such that every edge has at least one endpoint in the set (a vertex cover). Example: {a}

defaultSolver.solverDefinition: This solver simply tests combinations of nodes of size k until a solution is found, or all combinations are tested.

defaultVerifier.verifierDefinition: This is a Vertex Cover Verifier.

defaultVisualization.visualizationDefinition: This is a default visualization for Vertex Cover

solver.solverDefinition: This solver simply tests combinations of nodes of size k until a solution is found, or all combinations are tested.
